findings.title: Controls Over Cash Receipts Were Not Sufficient
findings.description: Controls over the Institutions’ cash receipts, which totaled approximately $1.8 million in fiscal year 2008, were not sufficient because cash receipts were not always restrictively endorsed and recorded immediately upon receipt, and deposit verification procedures had not been established to ensure that all collections were subsequently deposited.
findings.recommendation: a. that all cash receipts be restrictively endorsed and recorded upon receipt; and b. that the initial record of all cash receipts be verified to validated bank deposit documentation by an employee independent of the collection and deposit functions, and that this verification be documented.

findings.title: Adequate Controls Were Not Established Over Corporate Purchasing Cards
findings.description: The Institutions lacked adequate controls over its corporate purchasing cards because the employee who ordered new cards also received them from the Department, and finance office personnel did not document reviews of cardholder activity logs as required for 61 of 64 tested transactions totaling approximately $81,000.

dollar_amounts.context: purchasing card expenditures in fiscal year 2008

findings.recommendation: a. that the employee who requests purchasing cards from the Department not also receive the cards, and b. that the reviews of the cardholder activity logs by the fiscal officer or designee are documented.

findings.title: Employee time records were not always signed and a duplicate payment was made to a former employee
findings.description: Employee time records were frequently not signed by the applicable employee, with 17 of 41 reviewed not signed as required. Additionally, a duplicate payment of $15,855 was made to a retired employee for unused leave during fiscal year 2008 payroll totaling approximately $57 million.

dollar_amounts.context: duplicate payment to a retired employee

findings.recommendation: a. that all time records be signed by the applicable employee, b. that the existing procedures be reinforced to ensure that future duplicate payments are not made, and c. that the Institutions recover any overpaid amounts regarding the aforementioned retired employee.
